title: Cholamandalam Financial Holdings Ltd - 504973 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Chola MS general insurance Q1 FY27: GWP up 6.7% to Rs 2,130 cr, combined ratio 120.4% with motor OD loss ratio elevated (80-86%) and no clear recovery timeline; industry fire pricing still soft.

summary.headline: Chola MS Q1 FY27 combined ratio rose to 120.4% with GWP up 6.7% to Rs 2,130 crore and motor OD loss ratio still elevated.
summary.overview: Chola MS (general insurance arm of Cholamandalam Financial Holdings) reported GDPI of Rs 1,860 crore (+2.6% YoY) and GWP of Rs 2,130 crore (+6.7%), below management's expectations. Claims ratio rose to 85.6% (vs 81.3%) and combined ratio to 120.4%, driven by motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims and a large fire loss (Rs 12.4 crore net). Profit before tax was Rs 116 crore on operating profit of Rs 71 crore. Management said the OD loss ratio is unacceptable and targets a high-70s level first, while the Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment remains unprovided pending review.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Largest line (~70% of book per management); portfolio grew ~5.7% in Q1, mainly commercial vehicles. Mix: private cars 48%, two-wheelers ~9.5%, commercial vehicles ~42.5%. Motor combined ratio 128% in FY26 vs 123% in FY25; OD loss ratio now 80-86% range per analyst framing, not disputed by management.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Portfolio declined 8.6% in Q1 vs industry fire decline of ~28%; Chola MS fire decline limited to 15.5%. Growth in marine, engineering and liability.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Growth moderate; decline driven by pricing corrections in PSU bank group platform and migration of business to retail platform. Claims settled within 30 days for 99%; NPS 73. Health is being rebuilt from the ground up.

guidance_outlook: OD loss ratio near-term target: bring it to high-70s, then progressively to mid-70s; management said it expects below 80% over time, with a couple of quarters needed for measures to show results.

Corrective measures across motor (new vs renewal mix, NCB focus, ACS control, repair vs replacement analysis) and health (product redesign, pricing revisions, SME push) expected to become visible over coming quarters.
Expects greater property pricing discipline after June NATCAT events; reinsurance market correction more likely at next renewal cycle.
Ind AS / IFRS transition effective April 1, 2027 (one-year IRDAI forbearance granted); no profitability impact estimate yet, preliminary observations possibly next quarter.
Industry CAT loss estimate of Rs 3,000-4,000 crore from multiple events in Gujarat, Assam, Jamshedpur and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance capacity for fire and engineering secured at start of FY27, described as comparable to leading private players.
Motor issuance platform rolled out across bank channel; workflow enhancements under way in motor claims.
Health network exceeds 13,000 hospitals via PSU bank retail health partnerships.
Readiness work ongoing for Ind AS, Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework and DPDP requirements.
demand_pricing: Industry GI premium growth ~8.3% in Q1 vs 8.9% a year earlier; motor and health led growth, fire under severe pricing pressure.
Industry combined ratio ~117.8% in FY26 vs 112.6% FY25; Chola MS 115.2% FY26 vs 110% FY25.
Motor TP is tariff-based; premiums do not keep pace with claims inflation and court award trends.
Inward reinsurance growth cited as a driver of GWP outpacing GDPI; sources are commercial-lines participation and group health.
GIFT City reinsurers cited as contributing to soft commercial-lines pricing; management expects limited sustainable lead-line capacity from them.

qa_highlights.question: Has any additional motor TP provision been made for the Supreme Court homemaker judgment, and what is the path for motor OD loss ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No provision taken in Q1 for the Supreme Court judgment; review petition pending. OD loss ratio not accepted as the new normal; immediate target is high-70s, then mid-70s over time. Management said the 84.4% motor figure cited by analyst was not confirmed in the call, and said OD loss ratio below 80% is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retail and group health decline when the industry is growing strongly?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health decline reflects virtually no gross-subsidy business left, standalone accounts required to be individually profitable, and PSU bank group platform pricing corrections with migration to retail platform. Focus shifts to multinational single-mandate clients, SME and GPA cross-sell.

qa_highlights.question: Is the claims ratio rise from new book or from reserve provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase reflects claims inflation assumptions in reserving (expected ULR), not pure reserve strengthening; motor TP is tariff-based so pricing lags claims cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is motor two-wheeler reduced and how does the Supreme Court ruling affect claims?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler reduction was deliberate given profitability; courts have not uniformly applied the Rs 30,000 threshold and evaluate cases individually. Solvency impact of an adverse outcome not quantified; reserves said to include margin for adverse deviation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IFRS/Ind AS profitability and ROE impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Implementation effective April 1, 2027 after one-year forbearance; no reliable estimate yet, special-purpose financial statements not yet filed with IRDAI. Preliminary observations possibly next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is inward reinsurance growth sustainable and what is the CAT and reinsurance renewal outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inward reinsurance comes from commercial lines participation and selective group health; sustainable only as underwriting appetite allows. Hours-clause structure means separate deductibles per event, so P&L impact could be larger, supporting pricing discipline; reinsurance softness more visible at next renewal.

risks_watch: Motor OD loss ratio (80-86% range) and whether it moves toward high-70s as guided.
Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment: review outcome and possible retrospective provisioning; solvency at 1.93x.
Reinsurance renewal terms after soft market and GIFT City capacity; loss of commissions or higher retention risk.
Health portfolio profitability and rebuilding of retail health capabilities; combined ratio of group health was flagged as a concern.
Ind AS transition from April 1, 2027, with impact on profitability and ROE still unquantified.
key_quotes: On the OD side, I would like to clarify that we do not consider the current level of OD loss ratio to be acceptable.
we are certainly not accepting the current OD loss ratio as the new normal, nor are we suggesting that a loss ratio in the range of 80% to 86% is sustainable
To answer your first question, we have not taken any provision during the quarter in relation to the Supreme Court judgment.
At this stage, there is insufficient clarity on how the matter will finally evolve.
We would prefer to complete our assessment before providing any guidance on these aspects.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and somewhat defensive: management repeatedly called the motor OD loss ratio unacceptable and framed the Supreme Court homemaker judgment as unresolved, with no provision taken. It was open on the commercial lines and fire pricing outlook, but declined to quantify the Ind AS impact or the solvency effect of an adverse judgment.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; GWP grew 6.7% YoY (GDPI +2.6%) below management's own expectations, and the margin fix (OD loss ratio to high-70s) relies on corrective measures expected to show "over coming quarters" with no specific capacity, orders or contracts quantified.
